sub: What this elective module is about — and what is expected of you

title: This Drone Flies Our Code
desc: The course aircraft — a DJI Mini 4 Pro, flown by ~400 lines of our own Kotlin

items: One button → it takes off, flies a mission, lands — entirely from code we wrote (Module 5)
By the end of this course you build on this — and can defend every line at the live demo

title: About the Lecturer
desc: Aviation and software — a lifelong combination

body.caption: First contact with aviation technology: the motorized ultralight my father built with his own hands, 1986.

items: Decades as backend developer, lead and architect — distributed systems, data pipelines, safety-relevant software
Universities, banks, insurance, government, automotive, transport networks, startups, medical — and aviation safety: exactly the mix air traffic systems demand

title: What You Will Be Able to Do
desc: Seven outcomes — each one is checked at the live demo, not in a written exam

rows: Apply the Safety & Testing gate to flight code: tests first, manual review, simulator, then props — and explain why AI-generated code makes it necessary
Place a drone and an operation in EU 2019/947: category, class, subcategory, and what that means for the pilot's liability
Describe an interface with OpenAPI and generate client and server from it
Build a reactive telemetry pipeline — WebFlux ingest, topic fan-out, CQRS state — and contract-test every seam with Karate
Decode NOTAM and METAR by hand and explain what AIXM, ASTERIX and OLDI carry
Validate traffic logic in BlueSky and put live tracks on a moving map
Build, measure and defend your own increment on the DJI client

title: Semester Plan
desc: Nine sessions — lecture blocks in the morning, lab and project time after

rows: Lab: first flight in the simulator · project proposal due
Lecture · Karate against the demo service
table.note: Dates are fixed at semester start. Lab flight slots are booked separately — book early, flight time is the scarce resource (Module 4).

title: Course Organization & Grading
desc: Your graded deliverable: a hands-on drone-software project

rows: Your own increment on top of the DJI client, on hardware or in the simulator
Run it, change it on request, explain every design decision
What you built, what you measured, where the SDK stopped you
table.note: One project, three views of it. Weights are announced in session 1; the bar for each part is spelled out in Module 4.

body.card: Before session 2 — do this at home
items: ☐ Create a DJI developer account and an App Key (developer.dji.com) — approval can take a day
☐ Install Android Studio and clone labs/dji-hello-world; it must build before you touch a drone
☐ Start the free EU A1/A3 online course at the LBA — the personal licence behind every outdoor flight (Module 1)
☐ Skim the 16 project ideas (Module 4) — you propose one in session 3
Using Claude & Co. is allowed and expected — and AI output is treated as untrusted input
Flight code passes the Safety & Testing gate (Module 2): tests first, manual review, simulator — then props
At the demo you defend every line — code you cannot explain is graded as missing
And if it crashes anyway: you are the liable operator — personally. Module 2 shows what that costs
